# Process Brief: PM-10 Plan Scope Management

## Purpose

Define how the new Lead Lab web-app scope will be developed, accepted, traced, and controlled while the project moves away from the WordPress baseline.

## Why This Process Is Required

- The current project baseline still describes a self-hosted WordPress portal.
- The new delivery plan proposes a private web application with community, classroom, calendar, search, and member-management capabilities.
- The September 11, 2026 program deadline leaves little time for uncontrolled scope growth.
- Restricted access, private files, participant data, and video-link exposure create material acceptance and security consequences.
- The server stack, authentication approach, and several content decisions remain unresolved.

## Tailoring Factors

| Factor | Project assessment | Scope-control effect |
|---|---|---|
| Criticality | The application supports a live Lead Lab program and restricted participant content. | Require explicit acceptance evidence and a launch fallback. |
| Scale | One private Lead Lab community; small initial product, but several feature areas. | Use a focused single-product scope rather than a multi-tenant platform model. |
| Duration | Delivery is planned within 23 calendar days. | Use fixed scope gates and a hard feature cut-off. |
| Complexity | New application, authentication, private files, video embeds, server deployment, and participant testing are involved. | Require traceability and technical acceptance tests. |
| Approach | Proposed incremental MVP delivery. | Use a scope note, prioritized backlog, vertical slice, and staged acceptance. |
| Standards | No additional legal or regulatory standard is recorded; privacy and security handling remain open. | Record gaps and do not treat missing controls as acceptable by default. |
| Culture | Requester and IT team are responsible; LeadLab Director gives final approval. | Keep PM direction and final launch approval distinct. |
| Maturity | Existing WordPress records and a proposed web-app plan exist; no custom-app scope baseline exists. | Establish a new controlled scope record after approval. |

## Minimum Scope-Management Output

The PM-10 output must define:

- The authoritative scope record for the web-app MVP.
- The owner who maintains scope and requirements.
- How requirements become approved scope.
- How scope is decomposed into features and work packages.
- How scope is traced to acceptance tests.
- How scope changes are proposed, impact-assessed, approved, rejected, and recorded.
- Which authority approves the MVP baseline and which authority accepts the launch.
- The scope review cadence and feature freeze date.
- The fallback decision if the custom application misses a delivery gate.

## Proposed Acceptance Approach

The proposed delivery plan uses four acceptance gates:

1. Environment ready.
2. Technical vertical slice works.
3. Launch scope is feature complete on staging.
4. Security, participant testing, content readiness, backup, and IT support are complete before launch.

These dates and gates remain proposed until the PM approves the scope-management approach. Acceptance evidence should link each launch requirement to a test result and unresolved exception.

## Proposed Change Route

1. Capture the proposed scope change in the change log.
2. Identify the affected requirement, feature, deliverable, or exclusion.
3. Assess schedule, cost, risk, quality, security, and fallback impact.
4. Obtain PM direction before changing the scope baseline or backlog.
5. Obtain LeadLab Director approval when the change affects launch commitment, participant experience, or acceptance conditions.
6. Update the approved scope record, backlog, traceability, and test conditions.
7. Reject or defer unapproved changes visibly.

No scope change should be implemented solely because it appears in a conversation or draft plan.

## Planned Process Sequence

| Sequence | Process | Dependency |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | PM-10 Plan Scope Management | Establishes the scope, acceptance, and change-control approach. |
| 2 | PM-11 Elicit and Analyze Requirements | Uses the approved approach to confirm user needs and testable outcomes. |
| 3 | PM-12 Define Scope | Converts approved requirements into committed boundaries and deliverables. |
| 4 | PM-13 Develop Scope Structure | Decomposes the approved scope into a buildable backlog or work structure. |

## Open Inputs for Stage 02

- Whether the proposed web-app direction is approved as the project scope or remains a recommendation.
- The named PM or product owner for scope decisions.
- The existing server runtime and supported database.
- Participant count and participant-data handling rules.
- Required September program content.
- Exact acceptance authority for the MVP scope before the LeadLab Director review.
